A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E(3)-Pose research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–M are available and support reliable comparison, including material that moved or was renumbered.

before.justification: v6 reports original pose-estimation experiments, ablations, segmentation evaluations, and slice-prescription simulations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v8 retains these original empirical results and adds simulated-lesion robustness results in Figure 4b.

M1.justification: The segmentation-based translation estimator, equivariant rotation network, pseudovector parametrization, training loss, and inference procedure are unchanged. The lesion experiment tests an existing asymmetric ablation; Appendix M's rotational-symmetry extension was already present.

E1.justification: The four datasets remain Research-Fetal, dHCP, Clinical-Young, and Navigators. Section 5.6 and Figure 4b add evaluation on Research-Fetal volumes containing simulated lateralized lesions, extending test coverage to pathological-asymmetry scenarios without adding a real pathological cohort.

E2.justification: The evaluated external baselines remain FireANTs, EquiTrack, Fetal-Align, 3DPose-Net, 6DRep, and RbR, with unchanged adaptations. The motion-blind simulation comparator is retained, and the new lesion analysis reuses the existing no-pseudovector ablation.

E3.justification: Figure 4b introduces a controlled lesion-diameter sweep. Appendix E also revises the stated Navigator annotation procedure from manually correcting every volume to correcting a subset. This is a reported protocol revision; the PDFs do not establish that existing labels or experiments were recomputed.

E4.justification: v8 adds a targeted sensitivity analysis testing when lateralized lesions undermine the reflection-symmetry assumption and whether the asymmetric variant helps. Existing intensity and rotation perturbations, component ablations, segmentation analysis, training-efficiency analysis, and slice-prescription simulations are retained.

E5.justification: v8 explicitly reports Bonferroni correction for Wilcoxon comparisons in Appendix I and Figure 4, with corresponding updates to Tables 1–3 captions. Appendix E newly discloses averaging ten registration runs for annotations; this does not establish increased training repetitions. Existing standard deviations, confidence intervals, and Navigator hierarchical permutation testing remain.

E6.justification: Figure 4b adds results showing robustness to smaller simulated lesions and greater errors under severe asymmetry, where the asymmetric variant performs better. Table 1 removes the significance marker from FireANTs' Research-Fetal rotation error of 10.6 ± 24.5 degrees. Numerical values in Tables 1–9 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix J removes v6's Theorem 4 and its counterexample asserting that geodesic loss violates pseudovector symmetry; v8 instead states that it respects this symmetry. This is a substantive but localized mathematical revision. The core equivariance proofs and Appendix M's derivation remain.

C1.justification: The conclusion strengthens the tentative suggestion that the asymmetric variant may be more robust into a claim that it is validated as a fallback under simulated asymmetries. The central claims about equivariant, symmetry-aware pose estimation and clinical-domain generalization remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix J replaces symmetry violation as the explanation for geodesic-loss performance with explicit uncertainty and possible SVD gradient instability. The discussion also grounds the pathology limitation in lesion simulations and explicitly leaves evaluation on real pathological cases to future work.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly documents annotation screening thresholds of 8 degrees and 8 mm and alignment to manually annotated initial poses. Table 1 clarifies that the reported 0.3-second runtime includes segmentation. Architecture, training hyperparameters, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v8 adds four references: reviews of fetal ventriculomegaly and brain tumors, Vector Neurons, and work on rotation learning with uncertainty. These support the lesion analysis, equivariant-network background, and future work without substantially changing the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: Targeted edits refine contribution wording, consolidate the equivariance definitions, expand annotation prose, and revise the discussion and Appendix J. The consent statement moves from Appendix G to Section 5.1. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 gains a lesion-analysis panel and example images and is rearranged into two rows; Table 2 is relocated. v8 also adopts a compact page format with smaller outer margins and updated running headers. Other figures and table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v8 turns a previously speculative symmetry limitation into measured sensitivity evidence, reports multiple-comparison correction, and makes annotation procedures more transparent. Appendix J also acknowledges uncertainty about the geodesic-loss performance gap. These are useful, targeted improvements; the principal benchmark results remain unchanged, and real-pathology validation is still outstanding.
